title: Mlai senior domain finetune vs rag
topic: Mlai senior domain finetune vs rag
question: When should you fine-tune a large language model versus use retrieval-augmented generation to give it access to specific knowledge?
idealAnswer:
RAG is generally the better default when the need is to give the model access to specific, current, or frequently changing factual knowledge, since updating a retrieval index is far cheaper and faster than retraining a model

Fine-tuning is better suited to teaching a model a style, format, tone, or task-specific behavior, e.g. always responding in a structured JSON schema, or a particular domain vocabulary, rather than injecting facts

RAG reduces hallucination risk for factual questions because the model can ground its answer in retrieved source text, and that source can be cited, whereas fine-tuning bakes knowledge into weights with no traceability and can still hallucinate confidently

Fine-tuning has real costs, data curation, compute, risk of degrading general capability through catastrophic forgetting, that RAG avoids, but RAG adds its own system complexity, retrieval quality, chunking strategy, and latency from the retrieval step

The two are not mutually exclusive, a common production pattern combines both, fine-tuning for behavior and format and RAG for up-to-date factual grounding
